newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net assets rise to $4.457 bln.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net assets rise to $4.457 bln.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday that its net international assets, as of November 15, were $4.457 billion, compared with $4.411 billion on November 8.
The central bank said its net international reserves, as of November 15, were $15.801 billion, compared with $15.897 billion as of November 8.
It said the increase of $46 million in international assets in the week was due to:
- Net revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of $232 million
- Net sales of foreign currency to the federal government worth $158 million, mainly for foreign debt service payments

- A net loss of $28 million for a combination of factors, including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts of commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said the monetary base rose by 2.851 billion pesos to $66.328 billion pesos largely because of seasonal demand for bills and coins.

The balance of the government's deposits with the central bank fell by 6.23 billion pesos, mainly as a result of the transfer of funds by the treasury to federal entities and outflows to buy foreign currency to service the debt.

Central bank credit to financial institutions rose by 987 million pesos. The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks.
